findings.item: Left/right/two-sided QFT — non-commutativity source
findings.claim: The literature explicitly treats the QFT as non-unique because quaternion multiplication is non-commutative. Three variants exist: left-sided QFT (kernel on the left), right-sided QFT (kernel on the right), and two-sided QFT (kernel factors on both sides). This is stated in Bülow-Felsberg-Sommer (2001) ch. 8, and is confirmed in the matrix-form paper by multiple subsequent authors. The 2007 arxiv paper (2307.01836) explicitly states: 'There is a left-side, a right-side, or even a two-sided Fourier transform for quaternions' and cites the origin to Sangwine 1996.

findings.item: Q8 / Klein-4 group theory fact
findings.claim: The fact that Q8/{±1} ≅ V4 ≅ Z2 × Z2 (the quaternion group modulo its centre {e, -e = ±1} is isomorphic to the Klein four-group) is a standard, verifiable finite-group result. The centre of Q8 is Z(Q8) = {+1, -1}. The quotient Q8/Z(Q8) is isomorphic to Z/2Z × Z/2Z ≅ V4 via the homomorphism sending i→(1,0), j→(0,1), k→(1,1) mod 2, with kernel Z(Q8), by the First Isomorphism Theorem. This is confirmed in standard group theory sources (Wikipedia quaternion group article, Johns Hopkins algebra coursework). LENS NOTE: the framework's use of this fact to motivate 'a Klein-4 object's native spectral transform is the QDFT' is a framework-reading lens, not attributed to the DFT literature.
findings.citation: Standard finite-group theory. Wikipedia 'Quaternion group' article: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion_group (states: 'the factor group Q8/{e,ē} is isomorphic to the Klein four-group V'). JHU algebra problem set: https://math.jhu.edu/mathcourses/401/testsol.pdf (proves Q8/Z(Q8) ≅ V4 via explicit homomorphism). Groupprops wiki: https://groupprops.subwiki.org/wiki/Center_of_quaternion_group. No single primary research paper required; this is textbook-level finite group theory.

sonnet.cross_cutting:
MISATTRIBUTION CORRECTIONS (load-bearing for lodging):

(1) 'Sangwine mid-1990s colour image paper' is correctly attributed to Sangwine alone, not Ell. Sangwine (1996) is a single-author Electronics Letters paper. Ell is not a co-author of this paper.

(2) 'Sangwine and Ell 2000s QDFT + fast algorithm' does not map to a single paper. The main joint Ell-Sangwine algorithmic paper is the 2007 IEEE Trans Image Processing paper (DOI 10.1109/TIP.2006.884955). The fast complexified QFT paper (Said, Le Bihan, Sangwine 2008, DOI 10.1109/TSP.2007.910477) is three-author and does not include Ell. The comprehensive QDFT book is Ell, Le Bihan, Sangwine (2014, DOI 10.1002/9781118930908).

(3) 'Bülow late-1990s PhD thesis' — the institution is Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel (not Kiel University of Technology), 1999. The thesis title is 'Hypercomplex Spectral Signal Representations for the Processing and Analysis of Images'. A follow-on journal article by Bülow and Sommer appeared in IEEE Trans Signal Processing 2001 (DOI 10.1109/78.960432).

LEFT/RIGHT/TWO-SIDED QFT: The three-variant structure (left-sided, right-sided, two-sided) arises because quaternion multiplication is non-commutative: placing the exponential kernel to the left or right of the signal function yields different transforms. This is explicitly discussed in Bülow-Felsberg-Sommer (2001, op. cit.) and is standard across the literature. The 2007 arXiv paper 2307.01836 attributes the original QFT proposal to Sangwine (1996).

OFT NON-ASSOCIATIVITY HANDLING: The Błaszczyk 2020 paper (arXiv 1905.12631) explicitly states: 'Recall that the octonion algebra is non-associative, so it is necessary to note that the multiplication in the above integrals is done from left to right.' The OFT kernel in the Błaszczyk definition is the product of three exponential factors e^{-e1*2pi*f1*x1} * e^{-e2*2pi*f2*x2} * e^{-e4*2pi*f3*x3} applied to the signal u(x) with left-to-right association: ((u(x) * kernel1) * kernel2) * kernel3. The Parseval-Plancherel theorem holds for real-valued inputs but NOT in general for octonion-valued inputs due to non-associativity (Błaszczyk-Snopek 2017, confirmed in secondary sources). The imaginary unit basis elements used are e1, e2, e4 (not e1, e2, e3) — this specific choice is a convention load-bearing for the OFT definition.

FRAMEWORK LENS (not attributed to DFT/OFT literature): The reading that 'a Klein-4 object's native transform is the QDFT' because Q8/{±1} ≅ V4, or that 'the 1:3:7 Hurwitz/Cayley-Dickson ladder carries the octonion order-content', is a framework lens offered by this research arc. It is not asserted as established by any of the cited authors above, and must not be attributed to them.

findings.item: C3 - How the OFT literature handles octonion NON-ASSOCIATIVITY
findings.claim: The literature fixes a bracketing/association convention: octonion multiplication in the OFT integral is performed strictly LEFT-TO-RIGHT, and the foundational definition restricts to REAL-VALUED functions of three variables (Hahn-Snopek / Blaszczyk-Snopek), exploiting that real-valued functions decompose into components of different parity. Non-associativity (and non-commutativity) is controlled by (a) fixed left-to-right evaluation and (b) the real-valued-input restriction.
findings.citation: Direct PDF extraction from arXiv 1905.12631 (Blaszczyk): 'Recall that the octonion algebra is non-associative, so it is necessary to note that the multiplication in the above integrals is done from left to right.' and 'where octonion multiplication is done from left to right.' and intro: '...the previous research of Hahn and Snopek, who used the fact that real-valued functions can be expressed as a sum of components of different parity.'
findings.support: Verbatim from OA preprint: non-associativity handled by explicit fixed LEFT-TO-RIGHT multiplication convention; original OFT defined on real-valued functions of three variables. The 2019 generalization (1905.12631) extends to octonion-valued 3-D signals while retaining left-to-right convention. Directly answers (C) with quoted source text.

findings.item: D - Klein four-group V = Z2xZ2 equals Q8 modulo its centre {+/-1}
findings.claim: Standard elementary finite-group fact: the quaternion group Q8 has centre Z(Q8) = {1,-1} (order 2), and the quotient Q8/{+/-1} is isomorphic to the Klein four-group V = Z2xZ2. Equivalently Inn(Q8) = Q8/Z(Q8) = V.
findings.citation: Wikipedia 'Quaternion group' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion_group), verbatim: 'The center and the commutator subgroup of Q8 is the subgroup {e, e-bar}.' and 'The inner automorphism group of Q8 is given by the group modulo its center, i.e. the factor group Q8/{e,e-bar}, which is isomorphic to the Klein four-group V.' Corroborated by Groupprops 'Center of quaternion group'. Canonical textbook home: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed. (Q8 in 1.5).
findings.support: Verified verbatim on Wikipedia, corroborated by Groupprops. Elementary: |Q8|=8, centre order 2, quotient order 4, non-cyclic (Q8 non-abelian) hence Klein-4 (unique non-cyclic group of order 4). Could NOT page-verify the specific Dummit and Foote page (no OA page image); fact attested via Wikipedia/Groupprops, sufficient for a standard fact.
